# Shaping and proofing

Shaping builds the tension that becomes oven spring. Proofing is where it is spent or wasted.

## Sequence

1. **Pre-shape** — turn the dough out, round it loosely, rest 20–30 minutes uncovered.
2. **Final shape** — batard or boule, seam side up into a floured banneton.
3. **Cold retard** — **12–16 hours at 4 °C**, straight from shaping. Flavour deepens and a cold dough scores cleanly.

Beyond 18 hours the crust goes leathery and the crumb tightens. Under 8 hours you lose most of the scoring benefit and roughly half the sour note.

## The poke test

Flour a finger and press 1 cm into the shoulder of the loaf:

- **Springs back immediately** — under-proofed. Give it 30–45 minutes at room temperature.
- **Springs back halfway in about 3 seconds** — ready. Bake it.
- **Does not spring back at all** — over-proofed. Bake it cold and flat; there is no rescue.

A dough that finished [bulk fermentation](bulk-fermentation.md) at a true 50 % rise almost always reads correctly on this test. If it never firms up in the fridge, the bulk went long, or the dough was slacker than the [hydration](hydration.md) page's numbers assume.

Score straight from the fridge and load immediately — see [bake and crust](bake-and-crust.md).
